title: When the Regiment Sings
premise: In the coastal city of Saltmere, Wren Thornbury has survived nine years of indenture to the Corvane Trading Company by keeping her hands busy and her face forgettable, measuring everything in what can be carried. When an infant is left at the workshop door with orders to 'forget the face,' Wren recognizes the child as the daughter of a diver who died in company waters, and the quiet arithmetic of her survival begins to fail. As armistice negotiations stall and the company prepares to burn its records, Wren must choose between finishing the ledger work that will buy her freedom papers and preserving the names the company wants erased, including her own true family name. She smuggles the child and the stolen register out on the last tide before the workshop burns, ending the war invisible no longer but finally carrying something that cannot be taken.
about_author: Freya Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading ledgers before turning to fiction. Her novels examine the small hands that hold large histories, and she writes from a house within earshot of working harbors.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We learn the rules of her invisibility: count what can be carried, never meet a patron's eyes, finish the work. The Corvane workshop hums with war contracts while divers' families wait outside for wages that never come. Emotional beat: uneasy competence — Wren believes her system of forgetting keeps everyone safe, including herself.

chapters.title: Instructions to Forget
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. An infant is left at the door at dawn with a note ordering the face forgotten; Wren recognizes the pearl-shell charm as belonging to Maren, a diver lost in company waters. Hiding the child inside the counting room, she falsifies a supply entry to explain extra rations. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve — the first crack in her practiced blindness.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, with interludes from the workshop foreman Bram, who suspects her. With armistice talks collapsing, Corvane orders all records burned; Wren discovers the register lists dead divers as deserters, erasing their families' claims. She copies names by candlelight while the child sleeps beneath her table. Emotional beat: rising dread and fierce purpose — memory itself becomes contraband.

chapters.title: The Last Tide
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the night before the burning, Bram corners her; instead of betraying her, he reveals he once lost a brother to the same ledger and covers her escape. Wren carries the child and the register through smoke-filled streets to a fishing boat, surrendering her freedom papers to buy passage. Emotional beat: catharsis — she leaves carrying more than she ever measured, and it is enough.
